reason: I'll start with the cut, since the rough edge needs to break the skin and vessel before platelets can plug it.
expectation: I expect a break in the skin and a small blood vessel, giving the platelets a place to gather.

alternatives.reason: The label explains that enzymes help form reinforcing threads, but I want to create the break first.

effect: The cut reaches a small leaking vessel, so platelets now have a break to plug.
reaction: The cut was what I expected; seeing the other skin parts stay in place makes it easier to follow.
reason: I'll gather platelets at the leaking vessel first, as the goal describes.
expectation: I expect the platelets to stick together at the break and form a plug, though it may still need reinforcing.

alternatives.reason: The enzyme label explains that it helps make reinforcing threads, but I want to make the plug first.

effect: The platelet plug slows the leak, but the surface cut remains open. The reinforcing threads are still needed.
reaction: Seeing the difference between slowing the leak and closing the surface was useful.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and the enzyme label says it helps the clotting protein form threads.
expectation: I expect reinforcing threads to form from the dissolved protein, though they may need a separate step to join the plug.

effect: The clotting proteins formed a mesh, and the next goal is to stop the bleeding.
reaction: The branching mesh makes the idea of reinforcement clearer.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and adding the threads to the platelet plug should reinforce it.
expectation: I expect the mesh to strengthen the plug and stop the bleeding, though the surface cut may remain open.

effect: The reinforced plug stopped the bleeding, but the skin surface still needs to heal.
reaction: It was useful to see that stopping bleeding and healing the cut are different things.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the protein mesh to the platelet plug was most worthwhile because it showed how the plug is reinforced and the bleeding stops.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making the protein threads was less engaging on its own: it followed the only offered pairing and mainly set up the final combination.

surprise.text: The surface cut stayed open even after the bleeding stopped, showing that a clot is only the first part of repair.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt especially arbitrary. The enzyme pairing was explained by its label, although I followed the hint rather than understanding a detailed mechanism.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the open skin heals, since stopping the leak left that question unanswered.
